title: Symbiodiniaceae Enumeration in Ground Coral Samples Using Countess II FL Automated Cell Counter
author: Rowan McLachlan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bdc5i2y6
materials: Countess II FL Automated Cell Counter
Export files to a computer using a USB.

steps.title: Prepare Salt Water
steps.instruction: Prepare a saltwater solution for dilutions.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 250 ml of Milli-Q water into a glass beaker using a glass graduated cylinder.
Weigh 9 g of Instant Ocean sea salt (or sodium chloride powder) using weighing paper and a balance and add to the beaker.
Stir with a clean metal spatula until all salt has dissolved.

steps.title: Grind Coral Fragments
steps.instruction: Process frozen coral fragments into a fine, homogeneous paste.

substeps.instruction: Grind frozen coral fragments using a chilled mortar and pestle or within an ice-bath until a fine consistency is achieved.

steps.title: Weigh and Partition Ground Coral Paste
steps.instruction: Measure the total weight and create subsamples for enumeration.

substeps.instruction: Transfer all ground coral material into a pre-baked aluminum weighing pan and record the total wet weight of the ground coral fragment (grams).
Measure ~ 0.5 g of wet paste into a pre-labeled 15 ml polypropylene centrifuge tube (tube A).
Record the exact weight of the paste removed as the wet weight of subsample.
Store tube A in a -80 °C freezer immediately.
Archive remaining material in a 50 ml centrifuge tube at -80 °C.
Remove tube A from the -80 °C freezer.
Place in a room-temperature tap water bath for ~ 3 minutes or until fully defrosted.

steps.title: First Seawater Dilution and Separation
steps.instruction: Separate the Symbiodiniaceae cells and supernatant from the coral skeleton.

substeps.instruction: Add saltwater to tube A up to the 4 ml mark using a glass Pasteur pipet and dropper bulb.
Cap and vortex for 30 seconds, ensuring any material on the inner walls is dislodged (use a spatula or hand-shaking if necessary).
Centrifuge for 10 minutes at 4000 rpm.
Carefully transfer the supernatant and the non-skeleton layer (Symbiodiniaceae) from tube A into a pre-labeled 15 ml centrifuge tube (tube B) using a glass Pasteur pipet.
Keep the Pasteur pipet in tube B for reuse.

steps.title: Second Seawater Dilution and Separation
steps.instruction: Perform a second wash to ensure all cells are recovered from the skeleton.

substeps.instruction: Add saltwater to tube A up to the 4 ml mark.
Cap and vortex for 30 seconds.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 4000 rpm.
Transfer the supernatant and thin tissue layer from tube A into tube B using the same Pasteur pipet.
Discard tube A and skeletal remains.

steps.title: Resuspend Cells in Formalin
steps.instruction: Concentrate the cells and fix them with formalin.

substeps.instruction: Cap and vortex tube B for 30 seconds.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 4000 rpm.
Remove and dispose of all liquid supernatant from tube B without disturbing the cell layer.
Add exactly 1000 µL of saltwater using a 1000 µL capacity pipet.
Add exactly 200 µL of 10% formalin using a 200 µL capacity pipet.
Store tube B in a refrigerator in the dark (count within two weeks).

steps.title: Load the Reusable Slide
steps.instruction: Load the concentrated sample onto the Countess II FL slide.

substeps.instruction: Place a clean, grease-free coverslip on the counting chamber of the Countess II FL Reusable Slide.
Vortex tube B for 30 seconds, wait 5 seconds, and remove 10 µL of solution using a 20 µL pipet.
Gently pipet the 10 µL sample into inlet 'side A' via capillary action.
Vortex tube B again for 30 seconds, wait 5 seconds, and load 10 µL into inlet 'side B'.

steps.title: Capture Fluorescence Image
steps.instruction: Use the Countess II FL to capture high-resolution images of the cells.

substeps.instruction: Insert the loaded slide into the white slide carrier and push into the instrument until it clicks.
Switch the light source to CY5 by selecting the red circle.
Click 'Adjust' and use the sliding scale to set brightness (e.g., 30-60% for P. compressa, P. lobata, and M. capitata).
Zoom to the maximum value (400%) and adjust focus until cells are spherical (note: autofocus may over-focus by ~20 units).
Check the CY5 box in the 'Collect Channels' section and click 'Capture'.
Wait ~ 20 seconds for the count to finish.

steps.title: Save Images to USB
steps.instruction: Export the images for external analysis in ImageJ.

substeps.instruction: Insert a USB drive into the instrument.
Click 'Save' on the Results screen.
Edit the sample name using the keypad and click 'Enter'.
Set Result, Images, and Report file types to PNG (data will automatically save as .csv).
Wait ~ 40 seconds for the saving process to complete.

steps.title: Process Second Slide Side
steps.instruction: Capture the image from the second side of the slide.

substeps.instruction: Push the slide into the instrument to trigger the spring release.
Rotate the slide in the carrier so side B is positioned for reading.
Re-insert and repeat the capture and save process.

steps.title: Clean Reusable Slide
steps.instruction: Clean the slide between different samples.

substeps.instruction: Rinse the glass slide and coverslip with Milli-Q water from a squirt bottle.
Gently rub with a cotton swab, rinse again, and dry with Kimwipes™.

steps.title: Analyze Cells using ImageJ
steps.instruction: Quantify cells using ImageJ software to avoid algorithm errors.

substeps.instruction: Open the saved CY5 fluorescence image in ImageJ.
Convert the image to 8-bit greyscale (Image > Type > 8-bit).
Set the Rolling ball radius to 500.
Adjust the threshold (Image > Adjust > Threshold) to optimize cell visualization (e.g., values of 10 or 30).
Convert to mask (Process > Binary > Convert to Mask).
Apply Watershed (Process > Binary > Watershed) to separate adjacent cells.
Click 'Analyze Particles' (Analyze > Analyze Particles).
Set the size range (e.g., 10 - 1000 pixel^2 for Hawaiian corals), select 'Outlines' from the Show menu, and check 'Exclude on edges'.
Confirm counts by comparing the outlines window with the 8-bit image using Ctrl + Scroll to zoom.

steps.title: Perform Replicates and Calculate Density
steps.instruction: Repeat the process for replicates and calculate final cell density.

substeps.instruction: Conduct four replicates per coral sample (two slides, two sides each) and average the cell counts.
Calculate total cells in tube B: Total # cells = (Average # cells ÷ 0.4 µL) x 1200 µL.
Calculate subsample surface area: SA subsample (cm²) = (wet weight of subsample (g) ÷ total wet weight of ground coral fragment (g)) x SA whole colony (cm²).
Calculate final density: Symbiodiniaceae density (# cells / cm²) = Total # cells in tube B ÷ SA subsample (cm²).
